subject: Re: Project Kestrel kickoff: CFQ classification guardrail
body:
Hi both,

Status: datasets are built for the primary CFQ split — rule-based negatives and model negatives from the beam outputs of all three baselines. Classifier results, first pass: without annotations the sentence-pair model sits at 71.4% accuracy on the compositional test split; with structure annotations it reaches 79.8% — a +8.4-point lift, consistent with the paper's core claim that structure is what the vanilla model is missing.

The interesting operational finding: model negatives are much harder than rule-based ones — training on them is what makes the classifier useful against real parser errors.

Risk/trade-off: the tree-annotation pipeline (the xlink mapping dependency) remains brittle, and tree outputs only add ~1 point over flat structure annotations. Recommend we not put trees on the critical path for the integration recommendation.

Linnea
